summary: The solver achieved a perfect score of 100/100 on all 20 test cases in iteration 1, fully confirming the main hypothesis. A branch-and-bound algorithm with Lagrangian LP relaxation solves every test case optimally within ~50ms. The control arm (greedy by value/combined-weight density) scored 0, confirming the optimization mechanism is essential.
key_points: h-main CONFIRMED: Branch-and-bound with Lagrangian relaxation scored 100/100, finding provably optimal solutions for all 20 test cases well within the 1-second time limit.

h-control-negative CONFIRMED: Pure greedy (v/(m+l) density) scored 0/100 — it couldn't even beat the NSA baseline heuristic, demonstrating that the 2D constraint interaction requires proper optimization, not a single density proxy.

The key algorithmic insight was Lagrangian relaxation of the volume constraint: ternary-searching the dual variable λ to solve a 1D fractional knapsack on mass with modified values (v_i − λ·l_i) yields the exact LP bound, tight enough (~1% gap) to make B&B with 12 item types practical.
Score is already at maximum (100). No further iteration is needed to improve the objective. The solution is stable across multiple judge runs.

If a next iteration were warranted, it would investigate robustness: (a) time-based fallback to greedy+local-search for adversarial inputs that could slow B&B, (b) alternative branching orders (e.g., smallest effective quantity first), (c) whether the Docker environment introduces any non-deterministic timing failures.
